extension.evidence.lookalike_letters: Some letters in the address only look like ordinary ones. That is how the real address is hidden.
extension.evidence.fake_brand_address: A famous name sits at the start of the address, but the site itself belongs to someone else.
extension.evidence.copies_brand_icon: The page shows a real company's icon but lives at an unrelated address — a common trick for stealing logins.
extension.evidence.no_https: Anything you type on this site is sent without protection and can be intercepted.
extension.evidence.missing_protections: The site skips basic protections that real companies normally set up.
extension.evidence.raw_ip_address: Real companies give their sites a name. Scam pages often use a bare number instead.
extension.evidence.unusual_connection: The site uses an unusual way to connect that ordinary websites rarely need.
extension.evidence.hidden_destination: The link hides the address it really leads to.
extension.evidence.very_new_site: Scam sites usually live just a few days, so a brand-new address is a warning sign.
extension.evidence.scam_words: The address contains words like “login” or “secure” that scammers add to look official.
extension.evidence.carries_personal_data: The link itself carries your email or a sign-in key. Anyone who sees the link can take them.
extension.evidence.long_complex_address: The address is long and tangled, so it's hard to see where it really leads.
extension.evidence.many_redirects: The link jumps through several sites before landing here — often to hide where it really goes.
extension.evidence.risky_ending: The address ends in a zone (like .xyz or .top) where scam sites are especially common.
extension.evidence.risky_registrar: The site was registered through a service that scammers often choose.
extension.evidence.random_name: The name looks like a random jumble — typical of sites churned out for one-off scams.
extension.evidence.detector_suspicious: Our detector, trained on thousands of real and scam sites, finds this one similar to the scams.
extension.evidence.not_a_real_business: The site has no working email. Real companies almost always do.
extension.evidence.shifty_setup: The site keeps switching the servers it runs on — a trick that makes scam sites hard to shut down.
extension.evidence.padded_address: Extra parts are stacked in front of the real name so it's hard to spot.
extension.evidence.shared_hosting: Anyone can make a site on this free service in a minute, scammers included.
extension.evidence.on_cleanway_list: Cleanway's own list of known scam sites includes this one.
extension.evidence.site_not_found: There is no working site at this address right now. Check the spelling.

landing.dns.page_title: Phishing-blocking DNS — one tap, no app
landing.dns.page_description: Install the Cleanway DNS filter in 30 seconds on iPhone, Mac or Windows. System-wide protection — no VPN, no app. On Android, use the free Cleanway app.
landing.dns.hero_title: Block phishing on every app — without installing one
landing.dns.hero_subtitle: Cleanway runs a phishing-blocking DNS resolver. Point your phone or laptop at it and every app on the device — Safari, Chrome, Mail, banking apps — gets the same protection.
landing.dns.hero_meta: Works on iOS 14+, iPadOS 14+, macOS 11+ and Windows 11. No VPN. Won’t drain your battery. On Android — the free Cleanway app.
landing.dns.ios_intro: Tap the button below on your iPhone or iPad. iOS will ask permission to install a configuration profile.
landing.dns.ios_step1: Tap “Allow” when iOS asks to download the profile.
landing.dns.ios_step2: Open Settings → General → VPN & Device Management → Cleanway DNS.
landing.dns.ios_step3: Tap “Install” twice, then enter your device passcode.
landing.dns.ios_unsigned_note: If iOS shows “Unsigned”, that’s expected — Apple’s signing program is paid and we’d rather not pass the cost on to you. The profile itself is unchanged whether it’s signed or not.
landing.dns.android_app_intro: On Android, protection comes with the free Cleanway app: it blocks scam sites in every app and tells you right away.
landing.dns.android_undo_body: Please switch it back: open “Private DNS” in Settings (on Samsung: Connections → More connection settings) and choose “Automatic”. This setup isn’t supported yet, and with it your phone may lose internet.
landing.dns.win_intro: Windows 11 supports DNS-over-HTTPS natively. Earlier Windows versions need a third-party tool like Cloudflare 1.1.1.1 — sorry.
landing.dns.win_step1: Open Settings → Network & internet → Wi-Fi → click your network → DNS server assignment → Edit.
landing.dns.win_step2: Switch to Manual, turn on IPv4, set preferred DNS to 1.1.1.1 with DNS over HTTPS “On (manual template)”.
landing.dns.benefits_heading: What does this protect me from?
landing.dns.benefit_1: Phishing links in SMS, email, and Telegram open as a “site not found” instead of a credential-stealing page.
landing.dns.benefit_2: Known malware command-and-control hosts are stopped before your phone can reach them — as long as they are on the list.
landing.dns.benefit_3: Brand-impersonation domains (paypal-secure-login.com) are blocked at the resolver level — your browser never even loads them.
landing.dns.benefit_4: Works on every app, not just your browser. WhatsApp links, banking apps, in-app browsers — all protected.
landing.dns.privacy_heading: Privacy — what we see and what we don’t
landing.dns.privacy_body: Cleanway DNS resolves the domain only. We never log the queries to disk, never send them to Sentry, never sell them to anyone. Queries stay in memory just long enough to answer the request.
landing.dns.privacy_logs: What we DO keep: an anonymous daily counter of total queries and total blocks, used to publish our quarterly transparency report. No domains, no IPs, no users.
landing.dns.layer_heading: Where DNS fits in your protection
landing.dns.layer_body: DNS is the widest layer — it protects every app on your device, not just the browser. It is also the shallowest: it can only block a domain that is already on our phishing blocklist. It cannot read a page, so on its own it will not catch a brand-new phishing kit the moment it appears, or a credential form hiding on a trusted-but-hacked site.
landing.dns.layer_extension: For that deeper protection, add the Cleanway browser extension. It runs the full per-page analysis on every site you open, spots look-alike login forms in real time, and warns you before you type a password. DNS covers the widest surface; the extension adds the deepest checks — together they cover both.
landing.dns.layer_generic: This is not a generic DNS filter. Cleanway DNS is tuned specifically for phishing and credential theft, driven by the same threat intelligence that powers the extension — not a repurposed ad-blocking list.
landing.methodology.page_description: How Cleanway measures its own phishing detection: the datasets, the script, and when a number is allowed on the site.
landing.methodology.hero_title: How we measure our own detection rate
landing.methodology.hero_subtitle: Every accuracy number we show points here: the data, the script, and how to re-run it yourself.
landing.methodology.why_p1: A detection rate is only worth something if you can see how it was measured. So we publish the script, the data sources and every weekly result.
landing.methodology.why_p2: The script runs every Monday against fresh phishing links from public feeds and a sample of legitimate sites. Results are committed to our public GitHub repository — including the weeks when the numbers look bad.
landing.methodology.results_unavailable: No benchmark snapshot is available right now.
landing.methodology.verdict_mapping_head: How each service's answer is counted
landing.methodology.verdict_mapping_p1: Services answer in different ways. We reduce every answer to dangerous, safe or unknown. Unknown answers (rate-limited, not indexed, error) are counted separately — neither right nor wrong.
landing.methodology.reproduce_p1: You need git and Python 3. The script downloads the same feeds, runs the same comparisons and writes the same JSON:
landing.methodology.cadence_p1: The benchmark runs every Monday at 05:15 UTC in GitHub Actions and commits its results to docs/benchmarks/. If recall drops by more than 5 percentage points from the previous week, the workflow opens a pull request that flags it.
landing.methodology.results_not_publisha: The latest snapshot ({date}) is too small to quote: {phishing} phishing links, {classified} of them with a Cleanway verdict. We show numbers only when a run has at least {min_phishing} phishing links and at least {min_classified} verdicts. Every weekly run, small ones included, is in the repository.
landing.methodology.results_snapshot: Snapshot: {date}. Sample: {phishing} phishing links, {legit} legitimate sites.
landing.methodology.fp_not_measured: We show no false-alarm rate for this run: too few real sites got an answer from Cleanway, or the sample holds only sites our server treats as safe without checking (see the caveats below).
landing.methodology.dataset_phishing_des: fresh links from the URLhaus and PhishTank public feeds, downloaded at each run and de-duplicated by domain.
landing.methodology.dataset_safe_desc: random domains from the Tranco top-1M list, ranks 100 to 100,000, with a fixed random seed so the sample can be reproduced.
landing.methodology.mapping_cleanway: Cleanway: "dangerous" counts as dangerous, "safe" as safe, "caution" as unknown.
landing.methodology.mapping_cloudflare: Cloudflare 1.1.1.1 for Families: a blocked answer (NXDOMAIN or 0.0.0.0 / ::) counts as dangerous, a normal answer as safe.
landing.methodology.mapping_virustotal: VirusTotal: dangerous when at least 2 of its vendors flag the link; a single vendor is ignored as too noisy.
landing.methodology.caveat_endpoint: Cleanway is measured through its public site-check endpoint — the same anonymous path a visitor uses — not through a privileged one. It measures our server's verdict, not blocking on the phone: the phone's protection blocks straight away only the sites on its list, so this number does not say how many of these links a phone would block.
landing.methodology.caveat_rate_limit: Right now the weekly run is slowed down by that endpoint's rate limit, so many links get no verdict and most runs are too small to publish.
landing.methodology.caveat_phishtank: PhishTank's free lookup often answers "not indexed" for fresh links because its database lags by a few hours, so its column often shows "—".
landing.methodology.caveat_gsb: Google Safe Browsing needs an API key; when none is configured for the run, its column shows "—".
landing.methodology.caveat_nxdomain: A domain that no longer exists also gets NXDOMAIN from Cloudflare and is counted as a Cloudflare block, which flatters Cloudflare on phishing domains that have already been taken down.
landing.methodology.caveat_latency: Response times are measured from the machine that runs the script (a cloud runner in the US or EU); from other regions they will differ.
landing.methodology.caveat_allowlist: Our server treats sites in the Tranco top 100,000 as safe without analysing them, and the sample of real sites above comes from that same range. So it cannot show how often Cleanway wrongly calls a less famous real site dangerous, and we publish no false-alarm rate from it. We will once the sample includes real sites outside that list.
landing.support.title: Support
landing.support.subtitle: Answers to common questions, and what to do if something goes wrong.
landing.support.email_hint: Please include your phone model and what happened.
landing.support.q_vpn: Is this a VPN that hides my traffic?
landing.support.a_vpn: No. Cleanway uses Android's VPN mechanism only to run a local filter on your phone that blocks scam sites in every app. It does not hide where you go and does not send your traffic through another country. To reach the sites it doesn't block, your phone looks up their names, as it would without Cleanway, with your mobile operator's or Wi-Fi router's DNS server — and only if that doesn't answer, with Cloudflare (1.1.1.1) or Quad9 (9.9.9.9).
landing.support.a_install: Download the app, open the file and allow the installation — the Android page walks through every warning you may see on the way. On the first run, tap "Turn on protection" and allow the connection Android asks about.
landing.support.q_off: How do I turn it off?
landing.support.a_off: Open the app and tap "Pause protection". You can turn it back on anytime.
landing.support.q_fp: A safe site is blocked — what do I do?
landing.support.a_fp: Open Cleanway, go to the History tab and tap that site. Then tap "Not a scam — allow it" and confirm. Cleanway will stop blocking the site on your phone. If someone on the phone is asking you to allow a site, it's a scammer. Hang up. Allow a site only if you are sure it is the real one.
landing.support.a_privacy: Sites are checked against the list on your phone. When a site needs a closer look, only its name goes to our server — not the full link and not who you are. The text of messages you check never leaves the phone. The full details are in the privacy policy.
landing.support.email_not_live_body: Our support mailbox is still being set up, so messages to support@cleanway.ai may not reach us. Please don't send anything important there for now. The answers below cover the most common problems.
landing.support.q_app_vpn: Another app asks me to turn off my VPN
landing.support.a_app_vpn: Some apps — banks, messengers, government services — refuse to work while any VPN is on, and to Android, Cleanway's protection looks like one. Open Cleanway, tap "Pause protection", use that app, then turn protection back on.
landing.support.q_no_internet: The internet stopped working after I installed Cleanway
landing.support.a_no_internet: First pause protection in Cleanway and check whether sites open. If you ever typed dns.cleanway.ai into "Private DNS" in your phone's settings, set it back to "Automatic" — that setting stops Cleanway from working and can cut off the internet.
landing.support.a_calls: Cleanway never calls and never sends links by text message. If someone calls or writes in Cleanway's name and asks you to install something, read out a code or switch protection off — hang up. It is a scam.

mobile.shield.disclosure.title: How the shield works
mobile.shield.disclosure.body:
Cleanway sets up a local VPN on your phone. That is how Android lets an app filter website lookups for every other app.

• The list of known scam sites is stored on your phone. Website names are matched here, not sent to us.
• Lookups we don't block go to your network's own DNS server — your operator's or your router's, as they do without Cleanway. If it doesn't answer, they go to a public resolver (Cloudflare or Quad9).
• No other traffic is read, recorded or redirected. It is not a privacy VPN and does not hide your browsing.

If Android asks you to allow the connection, tap "OK".

mobile.message.shape.payment_alert: This looks like an ordinary payment notice from a bank. If you didn't make this payment, call the bank on the number on your card.
mobile.message.shape.pickup_code: This looks like an ordinary parcel pickup code. Give it only at the pickup point or to the courier when you collect the parcel.
mobile.message.shape.public_alert: This looks like an official public alert, for example from the emergency services.
mobile.message.shape.safety_notice: This looks like a warning about scammers from a bank or a mobile operator.
mobile.message.link.blocked: On our list of scam sites
mobile.message.link.allowed: Not checked: you allowed this site yourself
mobile.message.link.system: Not checked: a shared service like Google — anyone can put a page there
mobile.message.link.shortener: Short link — you can't see where it leads
mobile.message.link.messenger: Opens a messenger chat — we can't check who is on the other end
mobile.message.link.dangerous: Dangerous site, according to our check
mobile.message.link.clean: Our check found no problems with the site
mobile.message.link.rate_limited: Not checked: too many checks in a row. Try again in a few minutes.
mobile.message.link.timeout: Not checked: our server didn't answer in time
mobile.message.list_missing: The list of scam sites isn't on this phone yet, so the links weren't compared with it. The list downloads while the “Every app” shield is on.
mobile.message.list_stale: The list of scam sites on this phone hasn't been updated for a while. It updates while the “Every app” shield is on.
mobile.message.advice.no_link: Don't open the link from this message.
mobile.message.advice.no_reply: Don't reply, and don't call the numbers in it.
mobile.message.advice.no_code: Never tell anyone a code from an SMS — banks, the police and government services never ask for it.
mobile.message.advice.no_money: Don't transfer or pay money because a message asked you to.
mobile.message.advice.no_install: Don't install anything from the link.
mobile.message.advice.call_yourself: Not sure? Call the bank yourself on the number on the back of your card — other organisations on the number from their official website.
mobile.message.advice.call_relative: Call your relative back on the old number you know.
mobile.message.truncated: The message is very long — only its beginning was checked.
mobile.message.error_failed: Something went wrong. This does not mean the message is safe — please try again.
mobile.message.error_unsupported: Checking messages isn't available on this phone. You can still check a link from it: Share → Cleanway.
mobile.message.privacy: The text is checked on this phone only and is not sent anywhere. History keeps only the result and the website names, never the text. To check a link, only the website name and a random install number that changes every day go to our server.
mobile.breach.title: Leaked password check
mobile.breach.subtitle: Some people use their email address as their password. This tells you if that has already leaked.
mobile.breach.scope_note: This is not a full breach report. Listing every breach an address was caught in needs a paid data source we have not connected yet.
mobile.breach.found_body: This address has turned up {{times}} times in lists of leaked passwords. If you use it as a password anywhere, change that password now.
mobile.breach.clear_body: This address has not turned up as a password in any leak we can see. It may still have been in a breach we cannot check.
mobile.breach.error_body: The check did not go through. Please try again in a minute.
mobile.breach.how_step_1: Your email is turned into a long code on this phone.
mobile.breach.how_step_2: Only the first 5 characters of that code are sent.
mobile.breach.how_step_3: The server sends back hundreds of codes that start the same way.
mobile.breach.how_step_4: Your phone finds the match on its own.
mobile.breach.privacy: Your email address never leaves this phone.
mobile.history.score_hint: A higher score means more risk.
mobile.history.empty_body: Every link you check shows up here. The list is kept on this phone only.
mobile.history.privacy: This list stays on your phone. When you check a link, only the website name and a random install number that changes every day are sent to our servers.
mobile.history.filter_hint.all: Everything Cleanway stopped or warned you about, and everything you checked yourself.
mobile.history.filter_hint.blocked: Sites Cleanway didn't let open, and dangerous links you checked yourself.
mobile.history.filter_hint.warned: Sites Cleanway warned you about, and links you checked that call for care.
mobile.history.filter_hint.checked: Links and messages you checked yourself.
mobile.history.filter_hint.sms: Messages you checked. The text itself is never saved — only the result and the website names.
mobile.history.truncated: Only the most recent events are shown.
mobile.history.empty_on_body: Protection is on. When Cleanway stops a dangerous site, it will show up here.
mobile.history.empty_off_body: Cleanway isn't blocking dangerous sites right now, so there's nothing here. Turn protection on and blocked sites will show up here.
mobile.history.empty_warned_body: Sites Cleanway warns you about, and links you check that call for care, will show up here.
mobile.history.empty_checked_body: Paste a link or share it to Cleanway — the result will show up here.
mobile.history.empty_sms_body: Share a suspicious SMS to Cleanway or paste its text. The text itself isn't saved — only the result.
mobile.history.detail.blocked_body: This site is on the list of scam sites — Cleanway didn't let it open.
mobile.history.detail.blocked_calm: You don't need to do anything: the site didn't open.
mobile.history.detail.warned_body: The link had already opened when the check showed that this site looks like a scam.
mobile.history.detail.warned_advice: If the page is still open, close it and don't type anything on it. If you already entered a password or card details, call your bank on the number on the back of your card.
mobile.history.detail.allowed_body: You marked this site as not a scam — Cleanway doesn't block it.
mobile.history.detail.allowed_removed_bo: Earlier you marked this site as not a scam. It is no longer in your allowed sites, so Cleanway blocks it again.
mobile.history.detail.allow_confirm_body:
If someone on the phone is asking you to allow a site, it's a scammer. Hang up.

Allow {{domain}} only if you yourself are sure it is the real site. Cleanway will stop blocking it. You can undo this in Settings → Allowed sites.
mobile.history.listed_a11y: On the list of scam sites
mobile.report.title: Weekly report
mobile.report.summary_note: Counted from the links you checked in this app over the last 7 days.
mobile.report.flagged_note: These came back dangerous, or worth a second look.
mobile.report.clean_body: Every link you checked came back clean.
mobile.report.empty_body: Check a link and it will show up here.
mobile.report.share_message: My Cleanway week: {{checked}} links checked, {{flagged}} marked dangerous. cleanway.ai
mobile.report.privacy: This report is built on your phone from the links you checked here. It is not sent anywhere unless you share it.
mobile.score.subtitle: You checked links on {{days}} of the last 7 days
mobile.score.ring_a11y: You checked links on {{days}} of the last 7 days — {{band}}
mobile.score.honesty: This is not a measure of how safe you are. It only counts the days you checked a link in this app.
mobile.score.fact.dangerous_detail: {{num}} of the links you checked this week
mobile.score.empty_body: Check your first link, and this becomes a count of the days you check.
mobile.score.privacy: Worked out on your phone from your own check history. Nothing is sent anywhere.
mobile.settings.sign_in_desc: Keep your settings on all your devices
mobile.settings.signed_in_desc: Signed in. Your settings sync to this account.
mobile.settings.sign_out_confirm_body: Checks and history stay on this phone. Settings stop syncing until you sign in again.
mobile.settings.plan_desc: Protection on this phone is free
mobile.settings.report_desc: A summary of the links you checked
mobile.settings.family_desc: Send alerts to people you care about, end-to-end encrypted
mobile.settings.skill_note: Used by the Cleanway browser extension to word its warnings. This app does not change its own wording yet. Saved on this phone, and to your account when you are signed in.
mobile.settings.skill_kids_desc: Short, strict warnings, with no button to open a dangerous site anyway.
mobile.settings.skill_regular_desc: The default. Clear warnings with a little detail.
mobile.settings.skill_granny_desc: Simple words, short sentences, no jargon.
mobile.settings.skill_pro_desc: Raw scores, threat types and technical detail.
mobile.settings.alerts_note: Cleanway never reads your clipboard or your SMS — only what you share with it yourself.
mobile.settings.push_desc: Cleanway tells you when it stops a dangerous site.
mobile.settings.auto_check_desc: Share a link or an SMS with Cleanway and it's checked at once. Always on.
mobile.settings.clear_confirm_body: This deletes every check saved on this phone. It cannot be undone.
mobile.settings.privacy_note: Your check history stays on this phone. When you check a link, only the website name and a random install number go to our servers. The number changes every day and is there so check limits can count per phone rather than per mobile network.
mobile.settings.sync_failed_body: We couldn't reach your account, so this change won't show on your other devices yet. It will sync next time you change it while online.
mobile.settings.clear_done_body: All saved checks were removed from this phone.
mobile.settings.clear_failed_body: Something went wrong — your history is unchanged. Please try again.
mobile.settings.allowed_desc: Sites you marked as safe. The shield does not block these.
mobile.settings.language_note: Choose the language for the app.
mobile.settings.language_reload_body: Please close and reopen the app to finish switching the layout direction.
mobile.settings.linkguard_note: When on, links you tap in most apps go to Cleanway first; the built-in browsers of Telegram and MAX open links themselves, unchecked. Known scam sites won't open. Other links open straight away while we check the site, and you'll get a warning if the check finds a danger — sometimes this takes up to half a minute.
mobile.settings.linkguard_on_desc: Known scam sites won't open; other links are checked right after they open.
mobile.settings.linkguard_off_desc: Right now links open without a check. Turn this on to check them.
mobile.settings.push_off_desc: Turned off in your phone's settings — you won't hear about blocks. Tap to turn them on.
mobile.settings.linkguard_on_desc_no_lis: Links are checked right after they open; the list of scam sites arrives once you turn on the “All apps” shield.
mobile.family.title: Family Hub
mobile.family.signed_out_body: Sign in to set up Family Hub. When Cleanway blocks a scam in a family member's browser, you get an alert — end-to-end encrypted, so not even Cleanway can read it.
mobile.family.load_failed_body: We couldn't reach our servers, so we can't show your family right now. Your family is still there — please try again.
mobile.family.no_family_body: Get an alert when a scam is blocked in a loved one's browser. End-to-end encrypted — even Cleanway can't read the alerts.
mobile.family.join_invalid: That invite is not valid or has expired. Codes match upper and lower case exactly — pasting is the safest way.
mobile.family.members_load_failed: Couldn't load the member list right now. It usually comes back on its own — check again in a moment.
mobile.family.invite_desc: Makes a one-time code and PIN. Send them by text or read them out. Both appear once — keep them where the other person can read them.
mobile.family.alerts_empty: No alerts yet. When Cleanway blocks a scam in a family member's browser, it shows up here.
mobile.family.alerts_load_failed: Couldn't load alerts right now. This does not mean there are none — please try again.
mobile.family.alerts_undecryptable: {{n}} alert(s) couldn't be read on this phone. They were sent to a key this device doesn't have.
mobile.family.modal_title: Share this with your family member
mobile.family.modal_desc: Both appear once. After this closes you can't see them again — make another invite if you need to.
mobile.family.join_network_failed: We couldn't reach our servers, so the code wasn't checked. Your invite is fine — try again in a moment.
mobile.auth.privacy: With or without an account: we check website names on our servers — never your passwords, messages, or browsing history.
mobile.auth.generic_error: Something went wrong. Please try again.
mobile.auth.not_configured: Sign-in isn't available in this build. You can use everything else without an account.
mobile.auth.otp_sub: Enter your email and we'll send you a login code
mobile.auth.err_code_wrong: Wrong or expired code. Request a new one.
mobile.auth.err_network: No connection. Check your internet and try again.
mobile.auth.err_rate_limited: Too many code requests. Please wait a little and try again.
mobile.auth.err_captcha: The security check didn't finish. Please try again.
mobile.auth.err_captcha_update: Signing in needs a newer version of Cleanway. Please update the app and try again.
mobile.onboarding.s1_title: Check anything before you tap it
mobile.onboarding.s1_desc: Paste a link, scan a QR code, or share anything suspicious straight to Cleanway. You get a plain answer and the reasons behind it.
mobile.onboarding.s2_desc: To check a link, our servers get the website name and a random install number that changes every day. Your passwords, message texts and full page addresses never leave your phone.
mobile.onboarding.s3_desc: On Android, one setup step blocks known scam sites in every app. Brand-new scams can slip past any blocklist — that's what the check button is for.
mobile.android_native.fg_channel_desc: Shown while phishing protection is active
mobile.android_native.block_channel_desc: Tells you when Cleanway blocks a dangerous site
mobile.android_native.allow_channel_desc: Where to allow a site Cleanway blocked
mobile.android_native.allow_moved_text: Sites can now be allowed only in the Cleanway app. If someone on the phone is asking you to allow a site, it's a scammer. Hang up. If you yourself are sure {{domain}} is the real site, tap here to open History.
mobile.android_native.blocked_text: {{domain}} is on the list of scam sites. It won't open.
mobile.android_native.warn_title: This site looks like a scam
mobile.android_native.warn_text: {{domain}} looks dangerous. If it is open, close it and don't type anything.
mobile.android_native.paused_text: Turns back on by itself at {{time}}.
mobile.reason.flagged_dangerous: Google flags this site as dangerous
mobile.reason.on_blocklists: On trusted scam and spam blocklists
mobile.reason.imitates_brand: The name imitates a well-known brand
mobile.reason.lookalike_letters: Uses look-alike letters to fool you
mobile.reason.fake_brand_address: A trusted brand name is hidden inside a fake address
mobile.reason.raw_ip_address: The address is a raw number, not a real name
mobile.reason.unusual_connection: Uses an unusual way to connect
mobile.reason.hidden_destination: Hides where the link really goes
mobile.reason.very_new_site: This site was created very recently
mobile.reason.scam_words: The address contains words scams often use
mobile.reason.carries_personal_data: The link carries your personal details in it
mobile.reason.long_complex_address: The address is unusually long and complex
mobile.reason.many_redirects: The link bounces through several sites
mobile.reason.risky_ending: Uses an ending that scams favor
mobile.reason.risky_registrar: Registered through a service scammers often use
mobile.reason.detector_suspicious: Our detector finds this site suspicious
mobile.reason.detector_safe: Our detector considers this site safe
mobile.reason.not_a_real_business: Not set up like a real company's site
mobile.reason.shifty_setup: The site keeps changing where it lives — a common scam trick
mobile.reason.padded_address: The address is padded with extra parts to hide the real name
mobile.reason.on_cleanway_list: On Cleanway's list of scam sites
mobile.reason.unreachable_abroad: Our server abroad couldn't open the site. Many banks and government sites block foreign addresses, so this alone is not a sign of danger
mobile.reason.checks_incomplete: Some checks didn't finish, so the verdict is less certain
mobile.reason.user_content_platform: Anyone can make a page on this service — scammers too
mobile.reason.on_device_list: On the list of scam sites on your phone
mobile.update.optional_body: A newer version of Cleanway is out. Update to keep your protection current.
mobile.update.required_body: This version is out of date. Update Cleanway to keep your protection working.
